artifacts.summary: 6-phase contract-text pass mandating detached + guarded lake build invocation across 8 lean-extension contract files plus a new long-builds.md anchor.

memory_candidates.content: When a contract change removes an implicit bound (e.g. mandating run_in_background to escape a 10-minute foreground timeout cap), audit what else that bound was silently enforcing before removing it. In the Lean build case the foreground cap was simultaneously (a) the cause of a livelock -- a cap-killed lake build caches no .olean, so retries restart at the identical module -- and (b) the only ceiling on how long redundant concurrent builds survived. Lifting the cap alone would have let ~10 duplicate builds run to completion instead of dying partway, making memory pressure strictly worse. The correct planning move is to pair the removal with a compensating mechanism (here, a flock-based project-granular build guard) and land both obligations in ONE pass over the affected contract files, not two -- a second independent pass over the same engine twins is exactly how twin-file drift is introduced. Corollary: a synchronous command-substitution call site can adopt a guard (which returns stdout/exit code through $(...)) even when it cannot adopt detachment, so 'route through the guard, carve out of the detachment mandate only' is often a third option better than either restructuring or full exemption.
